title: Spark pays SPK rewards for sUSDS supplied on Aave, spending emissions on a competitor's venue
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.2.2.2.1 lets Spark "activate a new SPK token pre-launch token reward airdrop program to capture other growth opportunities," and the live instance (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.2.2.1.1.0.6.1) points those rewards off-platform: "sUSDS supplies on **Aave V3 Main Market** are eligible to earn 7,239,130 SPK tokens per month," starting when the sUSDS market is onboarded there and running until SPK issuance.

Aave is simultaneously the upstream Spark owes a 10% revenue share to and a direct competitor to SparkLend. Paying users to deposit on it inverts the usual reading of a token incentive.

The logic only makes sense if the objective is adoption of the *asset* rather than usage of the *venue*. sUSDS is Sky's yield-bearing stablecoin, and its value to the ecosystem is a function of how widely it is accepted as collateral — being listed and liquid on the largest lending market is worth more than the same deposits sitting on SparkLend. Spark, as the Agent whose liquidity layer and savings products are denominated in that asset, benefits from its acceptance regardless of which venue hosts it.

So SPK emissions are being used as distribution spend, not loyalty rewards. The same anti-cheat structure appears — the formula deducts `Stablecoin_i Borrow Amount / Stablecoin_i Liquidation Threshold` summed across stablecoins — confirming that what is being bought is net sUSDS holding, not activity.

The exposure is that the deposits are not Spark's to keep. Incentivized liquidity on someone else's protocol leaves when the incentive ends, and the acceptance it purchased persists only if the market has independently come to want the asset.
description: A special program grants 7,239,130 SPK per month to sUSDS suppliers on the Aave V3 Main Market, treating token emissions as distribution spend for Sky's stablecoin rather than loyalty to SparkLend.
